introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2026. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. $\sin\alpha=1$ for $\alpha=90^\circ+360^\circ k$, so in $[0^\circ,720^\circ]$: $2\theta=90^\circ$ or $2\theta=90^\circ+360^\circ=450^\circ$.

Divide by $2$:

Calculate $f(x)=\cos x-\sin x$ for the four missing values (answers to $1$ decimal place, as in the printed table):

- $x=\dfrac\pi6$: $\cos\dfrac\pi6-\sin\dfrac\pi6=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-\dfrac12=0.366\approx0.4$.
- $x=\dfrac{5\pi}6$: $-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-\dfrac12=-1.366\approx-1.4$.
- $x=\dfrac{7\pi}6$: $-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}-\left(-\dfrac12\right)=-0.366\approx-0.4$.
- $x=\dfrac{5\pi}3$: $\dfrac12-\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\right)=1.366\approx1.4$.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $\mathbf{0.4}$ | $-0.4$ | $-1$ | $-1.4$ | $\mathbf{-1.4}$ | $-1$ | $\mathbf{-0.4}$ | $0.4$ | $1$ | $\mathbf{1.4}$ | $1.4$ | $1$ |

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) On a graph paper, taking 2 cm for $\dfrac\pi6$ units on the $x$-axis and 4 cm for 1 unit on the $y$-axis, draw the graph of $y=f(x)$ for $0\le x\le\pi$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
This question asks for a drawing; here is exactly what to draw.

**Scales.** $x$-axis: $2$ cm for $\frac\pi6$, so $x=\pi$ is at $12$ cm (marks at $0,2,4,6,8,10,12$ cm). $y$-axis: $4$ cm per unit, so the $y$-axis goes from about $-1.5$ (6 cm below the $x$-axis) to $1$ (4 cm above).

**Points to plot** (from the table, $0\le x\le\pi$):

| $x$ | $0$ | $\frac\pi6$ | $\frac\pi3$ | $\frac\pi2$ | $\frac{2\pi}3$ | $\frac{5\pi}6$ | $\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| distance along $x$ (cm) | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ | $12$ |
| $f(x)$ | $1$ | $0.4$ | $-0.4$ | $-1$ | $-1.4$ | $-1.4$ | $-1$ |
| height (cm) | $4$ | $1.6$ | $-1.6$ | $-4$ | $-5.6$ | $-5.6$ | $-4$ |

Join the points with a **smooth curve** (not straight segments). The curve starts at $(0,1)$, crosses the $x$-axis at $x=\frac\pi4$ (since $\cos x=\sin x$ there), falls to a lowest point $f=-\sqrt2\approx-1.41$ at $x=\frac{3\pi}4$ (between the points at $\frac{2\pi}3$ and $\frac{5\pi}6$, which have the same height $-1.4$), then rises again to $-1$ at $x=\pi$. (It is a cosine-type wave, because $\cos x-\sin x=\sqrt2\cos\!\left(x+\frac\pi4\right)$.)

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) From your graph, write down the minimum value of $f(x)$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The lowest point of the curve is read on the $y$-axis: about $-1.4$, reached between $x=\frac{2\pi}3$ and $x=\frac{5\pi}6$.

This agrees with the exact value. Since $f(x)=\sqrt2\cos\!\left(x+\dfrac\pi4\right)$, the smallest value is $-\sqrt2\approx-1.41$, reached when $x+\dfrac\pi4=\pi$, i.e. $x=\dfrac{3\pi}4$.

**Minimum value of $f(x)\approx-1.4$ (exactly $-\sqrt2$), at $x=\dfrac{3\pi}4$.**
